Benito Pérez Galdós, Trafalgar, translated by Clara Bell.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/benito-perez-galdos/trafalgar/clara-bell

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Benito Pérez Galdós, the author of the original Spanish work, died 1920.
- Clara Bell, the translator and annotator, died 1927.

First publication of the text used: 1884, the English translation (SE colophon: 'Trafalgar was published in 1873 by Benito Pérez Galdós. It was translated from Spanish in 1884 by Clara Bell.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the edition's rights statement (quoted below) places the text in the US public domain. The English translation was first published in 1884, before 1931.
- Country of origin (United Kingdom): the facts do not name the place of first publication, so the country is taken from the translator's British citizenship (Wikidata Q1091668, citizenship United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland), and the text is in English (en-GB). If the first publication was in the United States instead, the US rule settles the origin, because the text was first published before 1931. Copyright in the United Kingdom lasts life plus 70 years after the death of the last surviving person named above. The last to die did so in 1927, so the work entered the public domain there on 1 January 1998.
- Original work (Spain, first published 1873): Benito Pérez Galdós, the author of the original, died in 1920 (Wikidata Q189869, citizenship Spain). Spain's term is life plus 80 years for authors who died before 1987, so the original entered the public domain in Spain on 1 January 2001. No other country that could be the original's country gives a later end date than 1 January 2021 (life plus 100 years, for Mexico, from 1920).

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: 'Trafalgar was published in 1873 by Benito Pérez Galdós. It was translated from Spanish in 1884 by Clara Bell.'
- Wikidata Q189869 (Benito Pérez Galdós), P570 = 1920-01-04.
